content: 1. Mountain AD, Kirby RL, Smith C, Eskes G, Thompson K conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of powered wheelchair skills training for individuals who have experienced a stroke. This study was published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2014. 2. Ozturk A and Ucsular FD investigated the impact of a wheelchair skills training program for community-dwelling manual wheelchair users in Turkey through a randomized controlled trial. Their findings were published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2011. 3. Rice LA, Dysterheft JL, Sanders E, and Rice IM explored the short-term effects of transfer training among pediatric wheelchair users who use their wheelchairs full-time. This randomized trial was published in the Journal of Spinal Cord Medicine in 2017. 4. Rigot SK, DiGiovine KM, Boninger ML, Hibbs R, Smith I, and Worobey LA assessed the effectiveness of a web-based, direct-to-user transfer training program through a randomized controlled trial. Their study appeared in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2021. 5. Routhier F, Kirby RL, Demers L, Depa M, and Thompson K evaluated the efficacy and retention of the French-Canadian version of the wheelchair skills training program for manual wheelchair users in a randomized controlled trial. This research was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2012. 6. Sakakibara BM, Miller WC, Souza M, Nikolova V, and Best KL conducted a pilot study to determine whether wheelchair skills training could improve confidence in using manual wheelchairs among older adults. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2013. 7. Caro C and Cruz D performed an integrative literature review on the training of manual wheelchair skills. Their work was published in Cadernos Brasileiros de Terapia Ocupacional in 2020. 8. Harvey LA, Glinsky JV, and Bowden JL systematically reviewed the effectiveness of 22 commonly administered physiotherapy interventions for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in Spinal Cord in 2016. 9. Holden MK reviewed the use of virtual environments for motor rehabilitation, discussing their applications and outcomes. This review was published in Cyberpsychology & Behavior in 2005. 10. Keeler L, Kirby RL, Parker K, McLean KD, and Hayden JA conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of the Wheelchair Skills Training Program. Their findings were published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2019. 11. Kehrer AL, Barkocy B, Downs B, Rice S, Chen SW, and Stark S systematically reviewed interventions aimed at promoting independent participation among middle-aged adults with long-term physical disabilities. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation in 2022. 12. Kenyon LK, Hostnik L, McElroy R, Peterson C, and Farris JP systematically reviewed power mobility training methods for children. Their findings were published in Pediatric Physical Therapy in 2018. 13. McSweeney E and Gowran RJ conducted a scoping review on wheelchair service provision education and training in lowand lower-middle-income countries. Their work was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2019. 14. Tu CJ, Liu L, Wang W, Du HP, Wang YM, Xu YB, et al. systematically reviewed the effectiveness and safety of wheelchair skills training programs in improving wheelchair skills capacity. Their findings were published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2017. 15. Erren-Wolters CV, van Dijk H, de Kort AC, Ijzerman MJ, and Jannink MJ reviewed the use of virtual reality for mobility device training and its clinical outcomes. This review was published in the International Journal of Rehabilitation Research in 2007. 16. Worobey LA, Kirby RL, Heinemann AW, Krobot EA, Dyson-Hudson TA, Cowan RE, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of group wheelchair skills training for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation. 17. Kirby RL, Miller WC, Routhier F, Demers L, Mihailidis A, Polgar JM, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of a wheelchair skills training program for powered wheelchair users. Their study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation. 18. Worobey LA, Rigot SK, Hogaboom NS, Venus C, and Boninger ML investigated the efficacy of web-based transfer training on independent wheelchair transfers through randomized controlled trials. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation. 19. Van Der Scheer JW, De Groot S, Tepper M, Faber W, Veeger DH, Van Der Woude LHV, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of low-intensity wheelchair training on fitness, wheelchair skill performance, and physical activity levels in individuals with long-term spinal cord injuries. Their study was published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2016. 20. Worobey LA, McKernan G, Toro M, Pearlman J, Cowan RE, Heinemann AW, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of group wheelchair maintenance training for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2021.
